claude.method: transcript sum of usage over unique message.id vs the provider aggregate the client recorded in its cost-state line. The cost-state line is a live snapshot: it is exact where written after the last message and drifts on long or resumed sessions, so only the chosen exact session is used for the acceptance check.

dsh.note: only jobs that wrote progress.jsonl carry a worker counter; older jobs have no independent count

a.formula: calls: whole-file .py reads with file>=200 lines and file not in the session's edited set; tokens: their output chars/4. For files it did edit, median(file lines / lines of the largest edit region) is reported instead.

b.formula: shell-route calls in shell file read / shell search / shell list-stat, output chars/4.

c.formula: calls classified inline Python DB query, output chars/4.

d.formula: schema-probe calls whose command/target names a store documented in tasks/worker_context/schemas/*.md (the file stems), output chars/4.

e.formula: repeated = sum over sessions of (occurrences-1) per identical normalised shell command; tokens = chars of the repeats /4. Separate list: .py scripts run >=3x in one session.

f.formula: calls whose status/is_error/exit-code marks them failed; tokens = their output chars/4; top-15 signatures = class + 70-char command prefix.

g.formula: steps saved = sum over maximal runs of >=2 consecutive model steps whose calls are all read-only, of (run length - 1). Each saved step would also have re-sent the context, so the token value is the step's carry, reported as 0 here because it is already inside context-carry.

h.formula: calls before the first edit/write, per session, from the worker's own tool_calls_before_first_edit where present else counted from the transcript; seconds = first edit timestamp - session start.

i.formula: calls with measured output >10,000 chars; tokens = chars/4. Results truncated by the writer are a lower bound (see per-source truncated count).
